Learning simulators improve patients through self-play and libraries of past replies \cite{du2024llms,almansoori2025selfevolving,li2024agent}, and prompt optimisers such as GEPA \cite{agrawal2025gepa} and DSPy \cite{khattab2023dspy} tune the instructions.
Patient-Zero checks what a patient says against small, single facts from the case \cite{lai2025patientzero}; TalkDep grounds depression personas clinically \cite{wang2025talkdep}.
Marking by LLM judges is cheap but biased, for example towards the judge's own model \cite{zheng2023judging,zhou2025personaeval}.
Our model shares trust-locked memory and resistance with PatientAct \cite{sabour2026patientact}; the difference is that we keep the decision itself, not only the facts, outside the language model.

The Twin borrows ideas such as ``trust changes when expectations are not met'' from the computational programme of the Brain/MINDS Digital Brain project \cite{brainminds}, but it is not a simulation of the brain.

Prompted Big Five personalities show up in large models \cite{jiang2024personallm,serapio2023personality}, but self-report tests of a model's personality are unreliable: three equivalent prompts give significantly different scores \cite{gupta2023selfassessment}, re-ordering the questions alone moves scores by about a fifth of the scale, and a long conversation history makes small models less stable \cite{tosato2025persist}.

Instructions drift within about eight rounds of dialogue \cite{li2024instruction}; persona variables explain under 10\% of the variance in what simulated people say \cite{hu2024persona}; model size does not predict persona adherence \cite{samuel2025personagym}; and some traits, such as high psychopathy or low conscientiousness, cannot be prompted reliably at all \cite{lee2025trait}.
Multi-turn reinforcement learning improves consistency \cite{abdulhai2025consistent}, and interviews, not questionnaires, are the better way to test a role-playing agent \cite{wang2023incharacter}.

\section{Related Work} Sentence embeddings. Sentence-BERT made it practical to compare sentences by meaning with one vector each \cite{reimers2019sentencebert}; MiniLM showed that small, distilled models keep most of the quality \cite{wang2020minilm}; contrastive training (SimCSE, E5, the BGE family) is the current standard recipe for small general-purpose encoders \cite{gao2021simcse,wang2022e5,xiao2023cpack}.

Dense retrieval matches questions to passages the same way \cite{karpukhin2020dpr}, and benchmarks such as BEIR and MTEB showed that retrieval quality varies a lot from one domain to another and must be measured in the target domain \cite{thakur2021beir,muennighoff2022mteb}.

PAWS showed that models trained on easy paraphrase pairs fail on pairs that share words but differ in meaning \cite{zhang2019paws}; our problem is the reverse, questions that share no words but mean the same.

Chen et al.\ built chatbots validated by clinicians for depression interviews \cite{chen2023llmempowered}; PATIENT-$\Psi$ bases patients on expert cognitive models with six conversation styles \cite{wang2024patient}; PSYCHE builds a Mental Status Exam framework to evaluate assessment agents \cite{lee2025psyche}; PatientAct adds trust-gated memory, reactions and resistance \cite{sabour2026patientact}; PatientHub collects many simulators \cite{sabour2026patienthub}; Roleplay-doh lets experts steer a patient with written principles \cite{louie2024ro

Patients that learn. EvoPatient improves patients through simulated doctor--patient practice and a checked library of past replies \cite{du2024llms}; MedAgentSim and Agent Hospital evolve agents in simulated clinics \cite{almansoori2025selfevolving,li2024agent}.

Patients with bodies and voices. Design guidelines for psychiatric virtual patients predate language models \cite{dupuy2020guidelines}; recent language-model 3D patients include Voigt et al.\ \cite{voigt2025llmpowered} and SOPHIE \cite{haut2025ai}; SimPatient and MedSimAI add feedback on the student's performance \cite{steenstra2025scaffolding,hicke2025medsimai}.

Does it help? A randomised trial found that patient simulation with structured feedback improved students' clinical decisions \cite{brugge2024llm}; AI scoring of OSCE interview transcripts agrees with experts within one point 67--87\% of the time \cite{geathers2025benchmarking}; a 2026 meta-analysis supports AI virtual patients for psychiatric interview training \cite{kilincel2026meta}.
AI judges are cheap but biased \cite{zheng2023judging}.

\subsection{The Digital Twin} Each turn the Twin: \begin{enumerate} \item finds the memories the doctor's words touch, by keywords and by meaning, then applies the trust locks, so a locked memory gives only a sign of discomfort; \item reads what the doctor just did (empathy, judgement, jargon, a risk question and others), changes trust, updates how guarded the patient is by fixed rules, and makes a short list of allowed behaviours; \item makes one call to the language model, which may only choose among the allowed behaviours, and writes the behaviour and emotion before the words; \item checks
